question: Salt Satyagraha was associated with the:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Disobedience Movement.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Salt Satyagraha:-**

 
 
• **It is also known as the Salt March or Dandi March, was a significant act of nonviolent civil disobedience led by Mahatma Gandhi in colonial India. **
 
• The 24-day march, which lasted from March 12 to April 5, 1930, was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly. 
 
• **Gandhi and his followers walked over 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad to Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat, to make salt from seawater.**
 
• This act of defiance was a symbolic protest against the British Salt Acts of 1882, which gave the British government a monopoly on the production and sale of salt in India.
 
• The Salt Satyagraha had a profound impact on the Indian independence movement.
 
• It galvanized public support for Gandhi and his philosophy of nonviolence, and it brought international attention to the struggle for Indian independence.
 
• The march also inspired other nonviolent resistance movements around the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement:-**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement was a nonviolent civil disobedience movement launched in August 1942 to demand the immediate withdrawal of British rule from India.
 
• The movement was led by Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Satyagraha:-**
 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha was a farmer's uprising that took place in Champaran district of Bihar, India, in 1917.
 
• The farmers were protesting against the British indigo planters' exploitative system of forced cultivation and low prices.
 
 
 
• **Kheda Satyagraha:-**
 
 
• The Kheda Satyagraha was a nonviolent peasant movement that took place in Kheda, Gujarat, India, in 1918.
 
• The peasants were protesting against the British government's insistence on collecting taxes despite the widespread damage caused by a famine.
